newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle market quiet, bid $71 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle market quiet, bid $71 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet early Wednesday, but expected to trade at $72.00 per cwt sometime during the day, up $1.00 from last week's top prices, feedlot sources said.
Bids were light at $71.00, with cattle owners asking $72.00 to $73.00, they said.
Prices were expected to be buoyed by the ongoing shortage of finished cattle, sources said.
Supplies were tight following two weeks of feedlots selling cattle ahead of schedule to meet packer demand and to take advantage of current profitability.
Feedlot cattle prices also were expected to be bolstered by higher beef prices and moderate retail demand.
Choice beef prices Tuesday were quoted up $2.06 to $2.57 per cwt and up $0.54 to $0.99 for select-grade, with 163 fabricated loads reported sold, according to USDA.

Choice prices were stronger than select because of the shortage of well-finished cattle coming out of feedlots, sources said. Cattle supplies, however, were expected to gradually increase the next few weeks, which could temper beef price advances, they said.
